summary: One menu item that creates the manager, finds the registry and wires them together.
overview: The steps between "I imported a sheet" and "a label shows French" are: make a GameObject, add a LocalizationManager, find the registry, assign it, pick a default and fallback language. None of them is a decision — which is exactly the kind of thing a menu item should do for you.

Offered instead of a prefab for the same reason as the camera rig's one-click setup: a prefab could not find YOUR registry. The component is already plug-and-play on its own, so this is convenience rather than a requirement.
useCases: Setting up localisation in a new scene without looking anything up.
Checking whether a scene someone else built is actually wired — it is safe to run on a scene that already has a manager.
Getting sensible default and fallback locale codes instead of typing "en" into a project that is not in English.
whereToFind: Toolkit ▸ Localization ▸ Set Up In This Scene

walkthrough.name: Existing manager
walkthrough.what: Configured and selected rather than duplicated, so running it twice is harmless.

walkthrough.name: Registry
walkthrough.what: Assigned automatically when the project contains exactly ONE LocaleRegistry. With several it says so and leaves the choice to you; with none it tells you to import a sheet first.

walkthrough.name: Default / Fallback Locale Code
walkthrough.what: Both set to the FIRST locale in the registry, which is nearly always the language the game was written in — and always a better guess than a hardcoded "en".

walkthrough.name: Result
walkthrough.what: Logged in full: what it created, what it assigned, and what to do next.

gotchas.title: It deliberately does NOT create a registry when none exists
gotchas.body: An empty registry would let the scene look wired while every key rendered as a missing-key marker — worse than an obviously missing reference. Import a sheet first with the Localization Importer.

gotchas.title: It only handles the scene-level wiring
gotchas.body: Labels still need a LocalizedText each. That part is genuinely per-label work and nothing can guess which of your labels are meant to be translated.

gotchas.title: It will not choose between several registries
gotchas.body: A project with more than one LocaleRegistry gets a report and no assignment, rather than a coin toss that silently ships the wrong set of languages.
